text: Why can a receiver not simply use its own clock to sample an incoming bit stream?
choices: Clocks are too expensive to include in receivers
Separate crystals differ by tens of parts per million, so the sampling point drifts by a full bit within thousands of bits
Clock signals cannot travel over copper
explanation: A typical crystal is accurate to about +/-50 ppm, which at 1 Gb/s means the sampling point drifts a full bit period after roughly twenty thousand bits. The clock must therefore be recovered from transitions in the data itself, which is why a long run of identical bits is a problem.
